problem_text:
A logistics company is selecting packages to load onto a cargo drone. Available packages are:
* Package 1: volume 16 cubic feet, revenue $115
* Package 2: volume 18 cubic feet, revenue $92
* Package 3: volume 12 cubic feet, revenue $241
* Package 4: volume 15 cubic feet, revenue $32
* Package 5: volume 6 cubic feet, revenue $128
* Package 6: volume 26 cubic feet, revenue $213
* Package 7: volume 28 cubic feet, revenue $24
* Package 8: volume 10 cubic feet, revenue $157
* Package 9: volume 46 cubic feet, revenue $167
* Package 10: volume 42 cubic feet, revenue $32
* Package 11: volume 37 cubic feet, revenue $114
* Package 12: volume 20 cubic feet, revenue $258
* Package 13: volume 25 cubic feet, revenue $67
* Package 14: volume 40 cubic feet, revenue $188
* Package 15: volume 6 cubic feet, revenue $244
* Package 16: volume 24 cubic feet, revenue $124
* Package 17: volume 40 cubic feet, revenue $32
* Package 18: volume 7 cubic feet, revenue $193
* Package 19: volume 43 cubic feet, revenue $246
* Package 20: volume 13 cubic feet, revenue $168
* Package 21: volume 19 cubic feet, revenue $60
* Package 22: volume 50 cubic feet, revenue $11
* Package 23: volume 5 cubic feet, revenue $232
* Package 24: volume 13 cubic feet, revenue $263
* Package 25: volume 14 cubic feet, revenue $260

The drone's cargo hold has a maximum capacity of 402 cubic feet. Choose the package combination that yields the highest total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each package must be either fully accepted or rejected.
